title: What is inside the seal?
checkedAgainst: the Personal Agent Protocol draft 1.0 (in progress; as published on 2026-11-13), read and not run: `model.test.ts` holds the model to the rules and examples of its sections 4.1, 5.1, 5.2 (including Delegated keys), 5.3, 10.4 and 10.7, each test naming its section; once a header is verified, chapter 1's model decides what the account allows. There is no reference implementation to run against, and no real cryptography: a signature in the model is the name of the key that made it. It is also held to what the protocol itself publishes, copied on 2026-11-13 into `fixtures/poppy-official.json`: its delegations and Session JWTs have the claims and typ values of the Company kit's JSON Schemas and none the delegation schema forbids, and the values of spec.md's 5.2 examples; only the shortened keys, IDs and stand-in hashes fail the schemas' formats.

answer: Three links: the agent's URL publishes its keys, one vouches for a short-lived key, and that key seals each request

questions.question: A thief copies your whole exchange request, Session header and access token together, and sends it to GET /orders/ord_7Hk2 to read the order instead. What does example.com answer, and which claim stops it?
questions.answer: 400 invalid_session at htm and htu: the header was signed for POST /orders/ord_7Hk2/exchanges, and this is GET /orders/ord_7Hk2. A Session JWT covers one request, and only that one.

questions.question: shoes.example's own documents named example.com's cart URL, so the agent signed a header for that URL and sent it to shoes.example, which replays it at example.com. Every signature in it is genuine. What happens?
questions.answer: 400 invalid_session at aud: the header is addressed to https://shoes.example, and this is https://auth.example.com. The agent names the Company it verified in aud, so a header one Company collects is refused by every other.

questions.question: Your delegated key leaks while its delegation still has hours to run. What can whoever holds it do at example.com, and until when?
questions.answer: Sign headers as any User ID it knows, signed out only: the exchange gets 401, naming orders:write. A Company that remembers which User ID each key signed for refuses it for anyone but usr_Q7c1vK: key 9E421cSq has already signed for usr_Q7c1vK. At 07:00 nothing works: the delegation expired at 06:00:00, and it is 07:00:00.

questions.question: An exact copy of the agent's request arrives ten seconds after it, and another two minutes after it. What happens to each?
questions.answer: Where the Company remembers jtis, the copy ten seconds later gets 400 invalid_session (jti e1j3Vb has been seen already, so this is a copy); where it does not, 200. The copy two minutes later gets 400 invalid_session either way: the header was signed at 00:13:20, 120 s before 00:15:20, outside the 60 s window (section 5.3).

questions.question: Why does the agent sign your requests at example.com (usr_Q7c1vK) and at shoes.example (usr_m4Tz9P) with different delegated keys?
questions.answer: With one key, the two Companies could match you by its thumbprint or its delegation’s jti. With 9E421cSq at one and Lp0wF2Ux at the other they have nothing in common, and a leaked key exposes you at one Company only.

scenarios.name: The Company remembers: jtis and keys (optional)

steps.title: A seal from a stranger
steps.line: Predict: why should the shop believe this seal?
steps.caption: Your agent sends example.com the jacket exchange, sealed as in chapter 1. The shop has never met this agent and shares no secret with it. Still it must learn which agent sent this and which User it is for, without learning who that User is. Each line on the ticket is a claim the seal makes. What would make a copy of this seal useless to anyone else?
steps.picture: The chain behind the seal is not drawn yet; the wax on the ticket asks what pressed it. The ticket's seal says: iss https://agent.example/agent.json, aud https://auth.example.com, POST https://api.example.com/orders/ord_7Hk2/exchanges, sid Yx2b7Q, sub usr_Q7c1vK, signed at 00:13:20, jti e1j3Vb, ath covering the access token it carries; the request is POST https://api.example.com/orders/ord_7Hk2/exchanges with access token at_Qp4w. Nothing has been checked yet. The Company makes the two optional checks; it remembers no jti yet and no key yet. The agent has not sent its exchange yet. The rule, from section 5.3 of the draft: The Company verifies the Session header before it relies on anything in it.

steps.title: The sender’s name is an address
steps.line: iss is a URL that returns the agent’s keys.
steps.caption: Inside the seal, a claim called iss names the agent as a URL, https://agent.example/agent.json, and the shop fetches it. The document there must give that same URL as its client_id, and it lists the agent’s published keys on the same domain. Anyone can claim to be agent.example. Only agent.example decides which keys hang at that address.
steps.picture: Across the top, the agent's metadata document at its client_id, and its published key, qijAJ9BU, chained to it. The ticket's seal says: iss https://agent.example/agent.json, aud https://auth.example.com, POST https://api.example.com/orders/ord_7Hk2/exchanges, sid Yx2b7Q, sub usr_Q7c1vK, signed at 00:13:20, jti e1j3Vb, ath covering the access token it carries; the request is POST https://api.example.com/orders/ord_7Hk2/exchanges with access token at_Qp4w. Nothing has been checked yet. The Company makes the two optional checks; it remembers no jti yet and no key yet. The agent has not sent its exchange yet. The rule, from section 5.3 of the draft: The Company verifies the Session header before it relies on anything in it.

steps.title: The published key never touches a request
steps.line: It signs a short pass; the pass’s key seals.
steps.caption: Three links: the agent's URL publishes its keys, one vouches for a short-lived key, and that key seals each request. The published key signs a delegation: a pass lasting at most 24 hours, this one until 06:00, naming a delegated key and nothing about you or the shop. That key presses a fresh seal for each request. So the key all shops trust records nowhere which shops you use. Two signatures and an address: three links.
steps.picture: Across the top, the chain of vouching: the agent’s metadata document, its published key, a delegation lasting until 06:00:00, and the delegated key 9E421cSq, a stamp standing on the wax it pressed. The ticket's seal says: iss https://agent.example/agent.json, aud https://auth.example.com, POST https://api.example.com/orders/ord_7Hk2/exchanges, sid Yx2b7Q, sub usr_Q7c1vK, signed at 00:13:20, jti e1j3Vb, ath covering the access token it carries; the request is POST https://api.example.com/orders/ord_7Hk2/exchanges with access token at_Qp4w. Nothing has been checked yet. The Company makes the two optional checks; it remembers no jti yet and no key yet. The agent has not sent its exchange yet. The rule, from section 5.3 of the draft: The Company verifies the Session header before it relies on anything in it.

steps.title: Punched in order
steps.line: All 11 checks hold, two of them optional.
steps.caption: The shop walks the chain from iss down to the seal, then the claims: typed as a Session JWT, addressed to this shop, for this method and URL, signed a second ago, covering the token it carries. Then two optional checks: a jti it has not seen, and a key that has signed for no other User. 200. Some agents also sign for the network edge with Web Bot Auth; that replaces none of this.
steps.picture: Across the top, the chain of vouching: the agent’s metadata document, its published key, a delegation lasting until 06:00:00, and the delegated key 9E421cSq, a stamp standing on the wax it pressed. The ticket's seal says: iss https://agent.example/agent.json, aud https://auth.example.com, POST https://api.example.com/orders/ord_7Hk2/exchanges, sid Yx2b7Q, sub usr_Q7c1vK, signed at 00:13:20, jti e1j3Vb, ath covering the access token it carries; the request is POST https://api.example.com/orders/ord_7Hk2/exchanges with access token at_Qp4w. The agent sent the exchange, sealed, arriving at 00:13:21. Checks that held: header, client, delegation, signature, typ, aud, request, time, token, replay, one-user. Answer 200 OK. The Company makes the two optional checks; it remembers jtis e1j3Vb and key 9E421cSq signed for usr_Q7c1vK. The agent has sent its exchange. The rule, from section 5.3 of the draft: Every check passed: this agent, this User ID, this Company, this request, now.

steps.title: Copied to another address
steps.line: Another URL, or another shop: refused.
steps.caption: A thief copies the whole request, seal and token, to read the order instead: the seal says POST /exchanges, so 400 invalid_session. Next, shoes.example. Its own poppy.json named example.com’s cart URL, which nobody checks, so the agent signed for that URL with aud shoes.example. Replayed here, every signature is genuine, and aud refuses it. Look at who: you are usr_m4Tz9P there, under another key.

steps.title: The wrong hand on the seal
steps.line: Another agent’s seal, or the published key: refused.
steps.caption: A thief copies your access token and seals it with its own valid chain. The chain holds, as thief.example’s, but the token was issued to agent.example, so the token check refuses it. Then an agent seals with its published key directly. There is no delegation, so it is refused: a shop that took it would let the published key sign things that name you and a shop.
